messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: gpu-pool-west2a kernel OOM spike (metric: cuda.alloc.failures). Alert ID=PD-98421. sample: 
    nn_infer_worker_42: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
    stack: serving/runtime/kern_launch.cpp:142
  
pagerduty: PagerDuty: page fired to rotation 'eng-oncall' (severity: P2). Escalation in 2m if not acked. Incident details: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD-98421

oncall-erin: Acked. I'm on it, assessing. Where's the impact? :eyes:

megan-support: Seeing increased 5xx from hosted api in us-west: ~11% failures over last 3m. Most are 502/503 from the inference gateway, customers reporting slow/error. We have a couple customers with long-running batch jobs that spike mem.

sre-miguel: @oncall-erin tagging in. Quick plan: 1) throttle kvcache prefetch on that pool 2) move noisy customers off the pool 3) if needed, recycle worst offenders. Do we have a list of affected nodes?

ml-infra-kevin: Dumping recent alloc failure log for worker 42:
```
[2026-03-15T12:07:01Z] WARN cuda: alloc failed 134217728 bytes
[2026-03-15T12:07:01Z] ERROR infer: kernel OOM on stream 3
[2026-03-15T12:07:01Z] INFO autoshedder: prefetched 4GB in last 60s
```
Suspect aggressive prefetch + large seqs from customer X. kvcache prefetch config currently: `prefetch.parallel=8` on pool-west2a.

oncall-erin: Ok running quick mitigation: lowering prefetch parallelism to 2 on pool-west2a. Command: 
```
infractl pool update --pool pool-west2a --set prefetch.parallel=2
```
Applying now. Will monitor.

incident-bot: Command executed by oncall-erin at 2026-03-15T12:08:05Z: infractl pool update --pool pool-west2a --set prefetch.parallel=2

megan-support: After change: error rate dropped to ~6% within 45s. Customers with batch jobs still seeing intermittent fails but overall improved.

ml-infra-kevin: Suggest putting a temporary rate-limit on the heaviest customer to protect pool. On my side I can reroute some non-critical routes to gpu-lowmem variant.

oncall-erin: Kicking quick reroute for non-prod customers off pool-west2a to fallback pool. Command: 
```
routingctl shift --from pool-west2a --to pool-west2a-fallback --tag nonprod --percentage 100
```

incident-bot: routingctl: shift accepted; rerouting 64 workers.

pagerduty: Note: 1 escalation step suppressed (ack received).

sre-miguel: Taking over on-call handoff in 10m. I'll continue monitoring for 30 more minutes and follow up with root-cause triage. Initial RCA hypothesis: prefetch concurrency + large-sequence customer causing transient GPU memory pressure -> kernel alloc failures -> OOM.

megan-support: Customer-impact summary for postmortem: ~12% of requests to west region impacted for 12 minutes window (12:07 - 12:19). Affected customers: customer-X (batch), customer-Y (interactive heavy seqs). No data loss, retries succeeded for many, some batch jobs failed and were restarted. Support ticket numbers: #SUP-22411, #SUP-22412.

ml-infra-kevin: Followups I recommend: add soft-throttle for prefetch based on recent cuda.alloc.failures metric, add runbook step to reduce prefetch.parallel to 1 as a quick mitigation, and evaluate KV cache memory accounting in the runtime.

oncall-erin: Handing off to @sre-miguel for stabilization. Leaving logs + commands in incident channel. :thumbsup:

sre-miguel: Ack. Taking over. Will escalate to eng-infra if we see >5% error over next 15m. Logging timeline to the incident tracker.

megan-support: I'll update the affected customers and attach the mitigation notes.

incident-bot: Incident PD-98421: status=acknowledged, handlers=[oncall-erin, sre-miguel], pager_state=stable. Closing slack thread when resolved. :white_check_mark:
